about:
# ZoomPad

Big **+** and **-** buttons on screen that zoom the camera in and out. Made for playing World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.x) on a Steam Deck: tap them on the touchscreen. They work with a mouse too.

## What it does

Forever's controller mode zooms only while you hold both bumpers and push the right stick, which is awkward on a handheld. ZoomPad puts two buttons on the right edge of the screen, under your right thumb:

- **Tap** + to zoom in one step, or - to zoom out one step.
- **Hold** either one to keep zooming until you lift your finger.
- They only show once you **use a controller** (press a button or move a stick; a Steam Deck's own controls count), so they stay out of the way when you play with mouse and keyboard, even with a controller plugged in; so does the minimap button. Once shown they stay until you log out, so tapping the screen does not hide them. Turn that off in the options or with `/zoompad always`.
- **Drag** either button to move the pair somewhere else. Lock them once they are where you want them, so a drag can never move them by accident.

## Options

Click the spyglass button on the minimap to hide or show the zoom buttons; right-click it for the options. You can also type `/zoompad` (or `/zpad`), or use the addon's entry in the minimap's addon list.

| Setting | Command |
|---|---|
| Show or hide the zoom buttons | `/zoompad show`, `hide`, `toggle` |
| Only once you use a controller (on by default) | `/zoompad always` |
| Lock them in place | `/zoompad lock` |
| Show or hide the minimap button | `/zoompad button` |
| Button size: small, medium or large | in the options |
| How far each tap zooms: small, medium or large | in the options |
| Put the buttons back where they started | `/zoompad reset` |
| Zoom one step (for a macro or key binding) | `/zoompad in`, `/zoompad out` |

## Good to know

- On a Steam Deck, the touchscreen acts as a mouse, so a tap is a click. If Steam Input is set to a layout that turns touches into something else, switch the touchscreen back to "Mouse" (or "Direct touch") for ZoomPad's buttons to respond.
- The game's Max Camera Distance setting still decides how far out the camera can go.

## Controller

With a game controller, the **B** button closes the ZoomPad options, like the X and Escape do. While a window is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B goes back to whatever you have it set to. When a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with the window open.

## More from this author

Other small addons for World of Warcraft: Forever, all free:

- **[MouseTip](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/mousetip)** shows tooltips at your mouse cursor.
- **[GatherLog](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gatherlog)** remembers ore, herbs, fishing pools, skinning spots, chests and rares across all your characters, and guides you back to the best spots.
- **[RangeShade](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/rangeshade)** shades action buttons red when your target is out of range.
- **[JunkMate](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/junkmate)** sells junk and repairs at vendors, and warns when your gear is wearing out.
- **[AltGlance](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/altglance)** shows all your characters at a glance: level, gold, rested and where you left them.
- **[SwiftQuest](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/swiftquest)** accepts quests and hands them in as soon as you talk to the quest giver, without ever choosing a reward for you.
- **[SessionRecap](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/sessionrecap)** keeps a running tally of your play session: gold, experience per hour, quests, gathering and loot.
- **[MacroKit](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/macrokit)** adds ready-made macros for your class and spec, for all nine classes, and never overwrites your own.
- **[GamepadMacros](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gamepadmacros)** adds ready-made macros for controller and Steam Deck players: heal yourself, use a quest item, save and wear gear, leave a group, emotes.
- **[FDR - Flight Data Recorder](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/fdr-flight-data-recorder)** times every flight-master flight and counts your next one down to landing.

## Installing

Install it from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/zoompad) with the CurseForge app, or by hand: copy this folder into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\` as `ZoomPad`, restart the game, and enable ZoomPad on the character select screen.

## Developing

- `tools\Link-Addon.ps1` links this folder into the game's AddOns folder, so edits are live after `/reload`.
- `python tests/run.py` runs the tests (`pip install lupa` once). They run the addon in real Lua 5.1 against a fake of the game's API.
- `tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "..."` runs the tests and pushes to GitHub. GitHub runs the tests again on every push.

## Releasing

`tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "Release x.y.z" -Tag vx.y.z` publishes and tags. The tag makes GitHub package the addon, attach the zip to a GitHub release and, once the CurseForge project ID is in `ZoomPad.toc` and a `CF_API_KEY` or `CF_KEY` secret is in this repository, upload it to CurseForge.

Before each release: raise `## Version:` in `ZoomPad.toc` and add the version to `CHANGELOG.md`.

releases.notes:
# ZoomPad

## 0.3.4

- **Controller:** when a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with a ZoomPad window open (it used to stay on closing the window until the fight ended). It closes the window again once the fight is over.

## 0.3.3

- **Controller:** the B button now closes ZoomPad's window, like the X and Escape. While one is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B does whatever you have it set to again.

## 0.3.2

- The zoom buttons and the minimap button now appear once you actually use a controller (a button or a stick), not merely when one is connected: some PCs report controllers that are not being used. They then stay until you log out, so tapping the screen does not hide them.

## 0.3.1

- The minimap button also goes away while no controller is connected, like the zoom buttons. `/zoompad` still opens the options.

## 0.3.0

- The zoom buttons now only appear while a controller is connected (a Steam Deck's own controls count), and go away when you play with mouse and keyboard. The minimap button's icon is grey while they are away. Turn this off in the options, or with `/zoompad always`.

## 0.2.3

- Fixed: the minimap button drew no icon or border (wrong texture paths), so it sat invisibly on top of other buttons. It now shows its spyglass icon, and is put back at its starting place below-left of the minimap once.

## 0.2.2

- Fixed: the minimap button could keep following the mouse after a drag, and then move together with another addon's button sitting on top of it. It now stops the moment you let go.

## 0.2.1

- The minimap button now starts below and to the left of the minimap, instead of sitting on top of other addons' buttons. If you had not moved it yet, it moves there by itself. You can still drag it anywhere round the rim.

## 0.2.0

- A minimap button: click it to hide or show the zoom buttons, right-click for the options, drag it round the minimap. Its icon turns grey while the zoom buttons are hidden. `/zoompad button` or the options hide the minimap button itself.

## 0.1.0

- First version: + and - buttons on screen that zoom the camera, for the Steam Deck's touchscreen. Tap for one step, hold to keep zooming, drag to move, lock in place. Button size and zoom per tap can be set in the options (`/zoompad`).
